cards: Septimius Severus was Roman emperor from 193 to 211 CE, born in Leptis Magna in North Africa.
Cao Cao was a Chinese warlord and statesman of the late Han period.
Marcus Aurelius was Roman emperor from 161 to 180, ruling jointly with Lucius Verus until 169.
Tertullian was a Christian writer from Carthage in Roman Africa and the first major theologian to write in Latin.
Claudius Ptolemy was a Greek mathematician, astronomer and geographer who worked in Alexandria in the second century CE.
c. 100–c. 170 CE · Islamic Caliphates & Middle East
Galen was a Greek physician of the second century CE whose writings dominated medicine for centuries.
Suetonius was a Roman biographer and imperial official who served as a secretary to the emperors Trajan and Hadrian.
Simon bar Kokhba, born Simon bar Kosiba, led the Jewish revolt against Rome in Judaea from 132 to 135 CE.
Apuleius was a Latin writer, orator and Platonist philosopher from Madauros in Roman North Africa.
Arrian of Nicomedia was a Greek historian, philosopher and Roman official of the second century CE.
Marinus of Tyre was a Greek geographer and mapmaker of the Roman period, active around 100 CE.
Dong Zhuo was a Chinese general and warlord of the late Han dynasty.
Gautamiputra Satakarni was a king of the Satavahana dynasty of the Deccan in the early 2nd century CE.
Kanishka was the most famous ruler of the Kushan Empire, reigning in the 2nd century CE, probably from about 127, over lands from Bactria to the Ganges plain, with capitals at Purushapura (Peshawar)…
Suro is the legendary founder of Geumgwan Gaya, the leading state of the Gaya confederacy in southern Korea, near modern Gimhae.
Yajna Sri Satakarni was one of the last powerful Satavahana kings, ruling in the late second century CE.
late 2nd century CE · South & Southeast Asia
Antoninus Pius was Roman emperor from 138 to 161, adopted heir of Hadrian and adoptive father of Marcus Aurelius.
Ashvaghosha was an Indian Buddhist philosopher, dramatist and poet, regarded as one of the first great masters of classical Sanskrit poetry.
Cai Lun was a Chinese court eunuch of the Eastern Han dynasty who, as director of the imperial workshops, presented an improved method of making paper to Emperor He in 105 CE.
Cai Yong was a scholar, calligrapher, musician and official of the Eastern Han dynasty.
Clodius Albinus was governor of Britain who claimed the Roman throne in the civil wars after 193.
Huvishka was a Kushan emperor who succeeded Kanishka and reigned for about three decades in the middle of the 2nd century CE, when the empire stretched from the Amu Darya to the middle Ganges.
fl. c. 150–190 CE · Central & East Asia
Papinian was a Roman jurist of the late second and early third centuries CE, regarded as one of the greatest legal minds of the classical period.
Yuan Shao was a Chinese warlord of the late Eastern Han dynasty, from a family of high officials.
Julia Domna was a Roman empress, daughter of the high priest of the sun god at Emesa in Syria.
Pausanias was a Greek traveller and geographer of the 2nd century CE, probably from Asia Minor.
Sun Ce was a warlord of the late Eastern Han who conquered the lands south of the lower Yangtze in the 190s.
Sun Jian was a Chinese general of the late Han dynasty from the lower Yangtze.
Abgar VIII, called the Great, was king of Osroene, ruling from Edessa from about 177 to 212 CE.
Commodus was Roman emperor from 180 to 192, son of Marcus Aurelius, with whom he had ruled jointly since 177.
Gongsun Du was appointed governor of Liaodong in 189 as the Han dynasty disintegrated, and made himself its independent ruler from Xiangping.
Lü Bu was a Chinese warlord of the late Eastern Han dynasty, famed for his martial skill and notorious for betraying his patrons.
Lucius Verus was Roman emperor from 161 to 169 CE, ruling jointly with his adoptive brother Marcus Aurelius, the first time two emperors shared power as equals.
Rabbi Akiva (Akiva ben Joseph) was one of the leading Jewish sages of the early 2nd century CE, whose systematic teaching of oral law laid foundations for the Mishnah.
Sanatruq I was ruler of Hatra in northern Mesopotamia in the mid-2nd century CE and the first to take the title 'king of the Arabs'.
Sextus Julius Severus was a Roman general and senator from Dalmatia who governed Britain in the early 130s CE.
Yuan Shu was a Chinese warlord of the late Eastern Han dynasty and cousin of Yuan Shao.
Antinous was a young Greek from Bithynia who became the favourite of the emperor Hadrian.
Clement of Alexandria was a Christian theologian who taught in Alexandria in the late second century.
Pharasmanes II was a king of Iberia in eastern Georgia in the second century CE.
